turn_on.description: Set mode to a lit state (e.g. movie/effect).

methods.notes: Real discovery: UDP-broadcast to port 5555 a 1-byte 0x01 + ASCII "discover"; the reply carries the IP (reversed byte order), "OK" and the device id ("Twinkly_" + 6 uppercase hex from the MAC). Confirm with GET /xled/v1/gestalt.

device.name: Twinkly Smart Lights (string / curtain / matrix)
device.notes:
Twinkly are app-controlled decorative RGB/RGBW string, curtain and matrix lights. Control is a private-but-reverse-engineered local HTTP REST API on port 80 with a short-lived token, plus a UDP realtime channel on port 7777 for per-pixel streaming. No cloud is required for local control. Twinkly promised a public API that never shipped; xled documents the private one.
AUTH: POST /xled/v1/login with a random 32-byte base64 challenge returns a base64 authentication_token (8 bytes), a challenge-response and an expiry (typ. 14400s). The client must then POST /xled/v1/verify. The token goes in the X-Auth-Token header; a new login invalidates the previous token. The challenge-response is derived RC4-style from a key = device MAC XOR the 16-byte constant "evenmoresecret!!", then SHA1.
UNAUTHENTICATED reads: GET /xled/v1/gestalt (device details), /status, /fw/version.
CONTROL (token required): GET/POST /xled/v1/led/mode (off/color/demo/effect/ movie/playlist/rt), /led/color, /led/effects + /effects/current, /led/out/brightness (0-100), /led/out/saturation. Movies: POST /led/movie/full, /led/movies/current, /movies, /playlist. Layout: GET/POST /led/layout/full. All JSON replies carry an app code (1000 = ok); HTTP 401 on auth failure.
REALTIME: UDP 7777, three header versions — v1 (Gen I) 0x01 + 8-byte token + LED count; v2 (Gen II fw <= 2.4.6) 0x02 + token; v3 (fw >= 2.4.14) 0x03 + token + fragment number (frames fragmented up to 900 bytes).

openness.notes: The API is private but was reverse-engineered by the xled project; xled-docs is a complete unofficial specification. Newest firmware generations may differ — feature-detect.

upstream_docs.covers: The challenge-response derivation, UDP 5555 discovery and the UDP 7777 realtime header versions.

credentials.notes: Provisioning passes the home SSID/passphrase to /xled/v1/network/status over plain HTTP on the device AP. Control requires the per-session token, but that token is obtainable by any client that can reach port 80 and knows the device MAC (used in the challenge-response derivation).

factory_reset.description: One gesture across every generation of string, curtain and spritzer: the button has to be held while power arrives, so a user pressing it on a running set will see nothing happen. The colour the LEDs turn is the confirmation, and it differs by edition — red on the standard products, amber on the Gold Edition, which is the one detail likely to make someone release the button too early.
factory_reset.effect: Clears the stored WiFi credentials and returns the controller to its own AP for onboarding. Effects on saved effects and mapping are not stated by the vendor guides and were not tested.

procedures.basis: Twinkly's own quick-start guides for the LED string, curtain and spritzer products, which give the same three steps in every language edition examined.
procedures.indicator: All LEDs turn red — amber on the Gold Edition.
procedures.name: Controller button held while power is applied

steps.action: Unplug Twinkly from the power socket.
Press and hold the controller button.
While still holding the button, plug Twinkly back in.
Keep holding until all LEDs turn red (amber on the Gold Edition), then release.
steps.expect: Every LED lights red, or amber on the Gold Edition.

methods.description: Join the device AP ("Twinkly_XXXXXX") and use the REST network endpoints (/xled/v1/network/scan, /network/status) to hand it the home Wi-Fi credentials; it reboots onto the LAN.

steps.action: Power a new/reset device and join its 'Twinkly_XXXXXX' AP.
GET /xled/v1/network/scan then POST /xled/v1/network/status with the home SSID/passphrase.
steps.expect: The device reboots and joins the home Wi-Fi.

setup.notes: A factory-fresh device hosts its own AP ("Twinkly_XXXXXX"); the Twinkly app joins it to Wi-Fi. The same REST API can drive Wi-Fi onboarding: GET /xled/v1/network/scan, /network/scan_results, GET/POST /network/status. Not replayed here — low.

rejoin.notes: Wi-Fi can be rewritten through the /xled/v1/network endpoints while the device is reachable.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Endpoints, the login/verify token flow and the realtime UDP header versions are from xled-docs and the xled client (tested there on TW105S-EU and Twinkly 210 RGB+W).
